question: How is the Lord described as ruler of six wheels in the Traiśirasa doctrine?
premises: The Traiśirasa doctrine uses a reckoning of four, six, two, and two.
On that basis the Lord is said to rule six wheels.
This belongs to his wondrous own form.
inference: Different doctrinal reckonings present the same Lord as sovereign over specific wheel-configurations.
uncertainties: The internal arithmetic of the compound is compressed and tradition-dependent.
plain_english: In the Traiśirasa doctrine, by the reckoning of four, six, two, and two, the Lord—whose own form is wondrous—is said to have sovereignty over six wheels.
